feed.title: We made the bitcoin-dev mailing list readable: 15 years, 24,699 messages

entry.title: We made the bitcoin-dev mailing list readable: 15 years, 24,699 messages
entry.summary:
The archive of the Segwit2x mailing list is now available at [https://www.learnbitcoin.com/archive/lists/segwit2x](https://www.learnbitcoin.com/archive/lists/segwit2x). This comprehensive collection consists of 722 messages distributed across 75 threads, covering discussions from May 31 to December 1, 2017. The previous estimate of under 700 messages was found to be inaccurate after a recount of July's contributions. With the original Linux Foundation copy no longer accessible and no other mirrors discovered, this archive has been meticulously reconstructed using data preserved by the Wayback Machine.
To ensure accuracy in threading and Message-ID-based permalinks, monthly archive files were utilized for headers, while the content of each message was sourced directly from its archived page. This approach was necessary because the monthly files had replaced all non-ASCII characters with question marks, compromising text integrity. Every message in the archive includes a link to its corresponding Wayback capture, allowing users to trace back to the original snapshot. The structure mirrors that of the bitcoin-dev archive, featuring one page per thread and presenting messages as they were originally sent, without added summaries. Additionally, full integration with the archive search function is provided.
Two notable features enhance the usability of the archive. Firstly, any individual who contributed to both the Segwit2x and bitcoin-dev lists now has a unified people page, matched exclusively via email address to maintain consistency. Secondly, internal links within messages that previously directed users to the defunct lists.linuxfoundation.org pages have been reconfigured; these now open the relevant message within the new archive interface on both lists. Previously dead links are now functional, leveraging gnusha's redirector, although an entry for this list was absent during initial checks.
Contributors possessing an mbox file of the list are encouraged to share it for verification purposes, ensuring the fidelity of the reconstructed archive. Looking ahead, attention will shift to importing the lightning-dev mailing list, which shares the same archival format as Segwit2x. The lightning-dev archive is expected to be significantly larger, with approximately 4,000 messages spanning from 2015 to 2023. Community assistance through provision of an mbox or tarball would expedite and improve the accuracy of this process. Once completed, details about the lightning-dev archive’s availability will be announced in a dedicated thread.
